body:
SVG has the [`shape-rendering` property](https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/painting.html#ShapeRendering) (as CSS or an attribute) to address this kind of antialiasing issue. Specifically, the value `crispEdges` forces aliasing.

Adapted version of the fiddle, showing the regular SVG rendering (same as canvas) and the crisp edges version (the two triangles neatly fill the square): https://jsfiddle.net/g82ot9mc/

Of course, "crisp edges" create their own problems with jaggedy diagonal lines and curves. So you would never want to make that a default. But all the browsers have rendering code for SVG to swap to the aliased version, so it should be straightforward to implement — if the rendering requirements (and ideally, the terminology) match.

Note that I don't think any browsers currently do anything to distinguish between the other values of `shape-rendering` (`auto` vs `optimizeSpeed` vs `geometricPrecision`), but I haven't tested carefully.
